title: Family Services Center Guidance: Open Instrument Checkouts per Student and per Household (Fine Arts Instrument Usage Program)
content:
**Rule applied by the desk.** Under the Fine Arts Instrument Usage Program a household may hold instrument checkouts for any number of its students. An instrument is checked out only when the student holds fewer than the most open checkouts a student may hold at once under the usage type (the open checkouts being those in status checked out, in repair or overdue). A home-and-school pair under Large Instrument Usage (Tuba, Cello, String Bass) counts as one checkout and posts one usage fee.

## What is counted, and for whom

- **The household.** There is no limit on the number of checkouts a household holds across its students: one, two, three or more students of the same household may each hold a checkout.
- **The student.** The limit is counted for the student who would receive the instrument, from that student's own checkouts as the system records show them. A sibling's checkouts do not count toward this student's total.
- **Open checkouts.** A checkout counts as open while its status is checked out, in repair or overdue. A checkout in status returned or lost is not open and does not count.
- **The pair.** The two instruments of a home-and-school pair are one checkout, not two, and carry one usage fee, not two.

## Status of the student's existing checkout, read against the limit

The rows below take a usage type whose limit is one open checkout and a student who already holds exactly one earlier checkout:

| Status of the earlier checkout | Counts as open | Open checkouts held | Fewer than the limit | Within the open-checkout limit for another instrument |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| checked out | yes | 1 | no | no |
| in repair | yes | 1 | no | no |
| overdue | yes | 1 | no | no |
| returned | no | 0 | yes | yes |
| lost | no | 0 | yes | yes |

## Hypothetical cases

1. A household has three students in band and orchestra. Each student holds one open checkout. The household is within the rule: it may hold checkouts for any number of its students.
2. A student's woodwind instrument is at the repair shop and the student asks to take out a second instrument. The checkout in repair is open, so with a limit of one open checkout the student does not hold fewer than the limit, and no second instrument is checked out to that student.
3. A student holding Large Instrument Usage (Tuba, Cello, String Bass) has one tuba at home and one kept at school. The pair is one checkout, holds one place against the limit and posted one usage fee.
